## What this document does

Runs the testing checklist from `needle_litter_fS2_implementation_plan.md`
against the compiled C++ (`leaf_mass_correction = TRUE`, which now includes
the validated `fS^2`/`f_L`/`sLc` litter-pulse mechanism in
`actual_growth.cpp`/`growth.cpp`), not a parallel R reimplementation:

1. **trajectory** - the 15-year `leaf_mass` pool against its own yearly
   `N_repo(D,H)` target (Repola), bounded/no-NaN check.
2. **litter-timing** - daily `needle_litter` rate by day-of-year,
   2006-2016, confirming a single clean pulse per year (no double peaks),
   landing in the literature day 250-290 window.
3. **vs-observed** - that same model litter, converted to kg tree^-1 per
   real collection interval, against real SMEAR karike funnel trap data
   (`karike_df_all`, `neulanen` column), 2006-2016, with pine stand density
   interpolated from inventory years (same conversion as documented in
   `manuscript/paper_plan.Rmd`'s "Needle litter checked against real
   litterfall trap data" section, for the *old* pre-fS^2 mechanism - this
   reruns the same check for the new one).

```{r libraries}
devtools::load_all(quiet = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(patchwork)

pub_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.subtitle   = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey30"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position  = "bottom")

# Colour-blind-safe (Okabe & Ito 2008), used throughout this document.
okabe_ito_obs   <- "#0072B2"  # blue - observed/real data, points only (discrete samples)
okabe_ito_model <- "#D55E00"  # vermillion - CASSIA model output, line (continuous daily series)

# sLc_litter was fit via optimize() on pooled TRAINING years, checked
# against held-out VALIDATION years - needle_litter_fS2_implementation_plan.md.
train_years <- c(2006, 2008, 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016)
valid_years <- c(2007, 2009, 2011, 2013, 2015)
year_label  <- function(y) paste0(y, ifelse(y %in% train_years, " (fitted)", " (held-out)"))
```

## 1  Setup

### 1.1  Parameters

Same `h0`/`D0` overrides as `height_correction.Rmd`/`nitrogen_scenarios.Rmd`,
so this run starts at the same point (12m height) as the other Hyde-run
notebooks.

```{r setup-data}
data_directory  <- "~/Documents/CASSIA_Calibration/Processed_Data/"
loaded_data     <- load_data(data_directory)

new_parameters  <- rep(0.5, 27)
parameters_2015 <- initialize_parameters(calibration = FALSE, new_parameters)

parameters_2015$parameters_test[c("h0"),          "Hyde"] <- 12
parameters_2015$parameters_test[c("D0"),          "Hyde"] <- 0.1646
parameters_2015$parameters_test[c("GPP_mean"),    "Hyde"] <- 463.8833
parameters_2015$parameters_test[c("GPP_initial"), "Hyde"] <- 460.0
```

### 1.2  Weather data (1998-2022)

```{r setup-weather}
weather_preles <- data.table::fread("~/Documents/CASSIA/data/ERA5_CASSIA_preles.csv")

weather_1998_2022 <- weather_preles[
  weather_preles$date >= as.Date("1998-01-01") &
  weather_preles$date <= as.Date("2022-12-31"), ]
weather_1998_2022$dates <- as.Date(weather_1998_2022$date)
```

### 1.3  Pine stand density, interpolated across inventory years

Shared by Sect. 3 (real foliage biomass) and Sect. 4 (real litter) below.

```{r stand-density}
density_df <- loaded_data$smearII_data[
  loaded_data$smearII_data$variable == "tree density pine", ]
density_df <- aggregate(amount ~ date, data = density_df, FUN = mean)
density_df <- density_df[order(density_df$date), ]

density_interp <- approx(x = density_df$date, y = density_df$amount,
                          xout = 1997:2022, rule = 2)
density_by_year <- setNames(density_interp$y, 1997:2022)

dates_1998_2022 <- weather_1998_2022$dates
```

## 2  Run (leaf_mass_correction = TRUE)

`preles = TRUE` (not `photosynthesis_as_input`), same as
`height_correction.Rmd`/`nitrogen_scenarios.Rmd` - this matters here
specifically because `photosynthesis.fS` (which the new litter mechanism
reads) is only ever actually computed inside `preles_cpp()`'s daily call;
the `photosynthesis_as_input`/`phydro` pathways never touch `.fS` at all.

```{r run-model}
CASSIA_leaf_mass <- CASSIA_cpp(
  weather                    = weather_1998_2022,
  site                       = "Hyde",
  pPREL                      = c(parameters_2015$pPREL, parameters_2015$N_parameters),
  parameters                 = parameters_2015$parameters_test,
  common                     = common_p,
  ratios                     = ratios_p,
  sperling                   = parameters_2015$sperling_test,
  needle_mass_in             = 0,
  Throughfall                = parameters_2015$Throughfall,
  photosynthesis_as_input    = FALSE,
  nitrogen_balance           = 25,
  preles                     = TRUE,
  fAPAR_Tian                 = TRUE,
  organ_level_sugar          = FALSE,
  needle_mass_grows          = TRUE,
  height_diameter_correction = TRUE,
  leaf_mass_correction       = TRUE,
  root_turnover              = TRUE  # confirmed not to change needle_litter/leaf_mass (independent code paths, checked)
)

# CASSIA's needle_litter (and N_repo/leaf_mass behind it) is kg CARBON/tree
# - R/repola.R/src/repola.cpp both convert Repola's dry-mass allometry via
# "* carbon_share" with an explicit "# kg C / tree" comment. The real
# karike funnel-trap data (Sect. 2.3) is oven-dried mass (Karikkeet_readme.txt:
# "kuivapaino" = dry weight), with no carbon conversion applied anywhere in
# this notebook - so litter is converted back to dry-mass-equivalent here
# (divide by carbon_share) to match the real data's own native units,
# rather than converting every real dataset forward into carbon.
carbon_share_hyde <- parameters_2015$parameters_test["carbon_share", "Hyde"]

leaf_mass_df <- data.frame(
  dates              = dates_1998_2022,
  year               = as.integer(format(dates_1998_2022, "%Y")),
  day_of_year        = as.integer(format(dates_1998_2022, "%j")),
  leaf_mass          = CASSIA_leaf_mass$Growth$leaf_mass,
  litter             = CASSIA_leaf_mass$Turnover$needle_litter / carbon_share_hyde,
  root_litter        = CASSIA_leaf_mass$Turnover$root_litter / carbon_share_hyde,
  cone_litter        = CASSIA_leaf_mass$Turnover$cone_litter / carbon_share_hyde,
  branch_litter      = CASSIA_leaf_mass$Turnover$branch_litter / carbon_share_hyde,
  fS                 = CASSIA_leaf_mass$Preles$fS,
  diameter           = CASSIA_leaf_mass$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_diameter,
  height             = CASSIA_leaf_mass$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_height
)

cat("leaf_mass range:", range(leaf_mass_df$leaf_mass), "\n")
cat("any NaN/Inf in leaf_mass:", any(!is.finite(leaf_mass_df$leaf_mass)), "\n")
cat("any NaN/Inf in litter:", any(!is.finite(leaf_mass_df$litter)), "\n")
```

### 2.1  N_repo per year

`N_repo` is recomputed once per year (`CASSIA.cpp`) from **last year's**
Dec-31 diameter/height via Repola's `needle_mass` formula - the first
simulated year uses the initial `D0`/`h0` instead, since there is no prior
year. Mirrored here with the package's own `repola()` (R/repola.R), not a
re-derivation.

```{r n-repo-per-year}
years <- sort(unique(leaf_mass_df$year))

n_repo_of_year <- function(y) {
  if (y == min(years)) {
    d_prev <- parameters_2015$parameters_test[c("D0"), "Hyde"]
    h_prev <- parameters_2015$parameters_test[c("h0"), "Hyde"]
  } else {
    prev_rows <- leaf_mass_df[leaf_mass_df$year == y - 1, ]
    d_prev <- prev_rows$diameter[nrow(prev_rows)]
    h_prev <- prev_rows$height[nrow(prev_rows)]
  }
  # m.N.tot (carbon), not needle_mass (dry mass) - N_repo is compared
  # directly against leaf_mass (a carbon pool), mirroring the 2026-11-10
  # C++ fix (CASSIA.cpp's growth() call site) - needle_mass made this
  # target ~2x too large.
  repola(D0 = d_prev, h0 = h_prev, n.year = 1,
         needle_mas = list(0), ste = "Hyde",
         params = parameters_2015$parameters_test,
         reps = repo_p)$m.N.tot[[1]]
}

n_repo_df <- data.frame(year = years, N_repo = sapply(years, n_repo_of_year))
n_repo_df$start <- as.Date(paste0(n_repo_df$year, "-01-01"))
n_repo_df$end   <- as.Date(paste0(n_repo_df$year, "-12-31"))

print(n_repo_df)
```

### 2.2  Year-by-year mass balance diagnostic

Not exported by `CASSIA_cpp()` directly (`C_N_year`/`litter_boost_year` are
internal `growth_state` fields), but fully recoverable from the daily
`leaf_mass`/`needle_litter` series plus `N_repo`: annual litter is a direct
sum, annual growth is recovered from the mass balance
(`M_t = max(0, M_{t-1} - L_t + G_t)`), and the two correction factors are
then back-solved from `growth.cpp`'s own formulas
(`C_N_year = growth_total / (N_repo/n_age)`,
`litter_boost_year = litter_total / (N_repo/n_age)`, *given*
`rate_unnormalized` sums to `sum_degree_fL_last_year` as designed - i.e.
these are *implied* values, assuming no other confound).

```{r year-balance-diagnostic}
n_age <- parameters_2015$parameters_test[c("n_age"), "Hyde"]

year_balance <- do.call(rbind, lapply(years, function(y) {
  rows <- leaf_mass_df[leaf_mass_df$year == y, ]
  litter_total <- sum(rows$litter)
  peak <- max(rows$leaf_mass)
  trough <- min(rows$leaf_mass)
  net_change <- rows$leaf_mass[nrow(rows)] - rows$leaf_mass[1]
  growth_implied <- net_change + litter_total
  N_repo_y <- n_repo_df$N_repo[n_repo_df$year == y]
  data.frame(year = y, N_repo = N_repo_y, peak = peak, trough = trough,
             growth_total = growth_implied, litter_total = litter_total,
             growth_over_target = growth_implied / (N_repo_y / n_age),
             litter_over_target  = litter_total  / (N_repo_y / n_age))
}))

print(year_balance, digits = 3)
```

### 2.3  Real data: litter traps and foliage biomass (for Sects. 3-4)

```{r real-data-prep}
# Real litter-trap data (karike_df_all, needles) - used by Sect. 4.
karike <- karike_df_all  # lazy-loaded package data, not part of load_data()'s return list
karike$pvm <- as.Date(karike$pvm)
karike_recent <- karike[!is.na(karike$neulanen) &
                        format(karike$pvm, "%Y") %in% as.character(2006:2016), ]

real_litter <- aggregate(neulanen ~ pvm, data = karike_recent, FUN = mean)
real_litter <- real_litter[order(real_litter$pvm), ]
real_litter$year      <- as.integer(format(real_litter$pvm, "%Y"))
real_litter$fit_split <- year_label(real_litter$year)

# Collector geometry: 47.5cm-diameter circular funnel, area pi*0.2375^2 ~=
# 0.177 m^2 - close to Korhonen et al. (2013)'s own documented 0.2 m^2.
collector_area_m2 <- pi * 0.2375^2

real_litter$trees_per_ha <- density_by_year[as.character(real_litter$year)]
real_litter$kg_per_tree  <- (real_litter$neulanen / collector_area_m2) /
  (real_litter$trees_per_ha / 10000) / 1000

real_litter$interval_start <- c(as.Date(NA), head(real_litter$pvm, -1))
real_litter$interval_days  <- as.numeric(real_litter$pvm - real_litter$interval_start)
real_litter$day_of_year    <- as.integer(format(real_litter$pvm, "%j"))
real_litter$daily_rate_kg_tree_day <- real_litter$kg_per_tree / real_litter$interval_days

model_interval_sum <- function(start, end) {
  if (is.na(start)) return(NA_real_)
  sum(leaf_mass_df$litter[leaf_mass_df$dates > start & leaf_mass_df$dates <= end])
}
real_litter$model_kg_per_tree <- mapply(model_interval_sum,
                                         real_litter$interval_start, real_litter$pvm)
comparison <- real_litter[!is.na(real_litter$model_kg_per_tree), ]

# Real pine needle (foliage) biomass, CASSIA_Calibration/smearII_data -
# independent stand-inventory measurements, for Sect. 3's trajectory plot.
# Converted kg dry mass/ha -> kg C/tree (carbon_share = 0.5, matching
# leaf_mass's own units) using the same stand-density interpolation.
# Inventory dates are year-only, so each point is placed at 1 July of its
# year as an approximation.
foliage_df <- loaded_data$smearII_data[
  loaded_data$smearII_data$variable == "pine_foliage_biomass", ]
foliage_df <- foliage_df[order(foliage_df$date), ]
foliage_df$trees_per_ha    <- density_by_year[as.character(foliage_df$date)]
foliage_df$leaf_mass_kgC_tree <- (foliage_df$amount / foliage_df$trees_per_ha) * 0.5
foliage_df$dates <- as.Date(paste0(foliage_df$date, "-07-01"))
```

### 2.4  Three photosynthesis-model runs (SPP, PRELES, p-hydro) for litter comparison

Until 2026-11-10, `photosynthesis.fS` - which the `fS^2` needle-litter
mechanism reads - was only ever computed inside `preles_cpp()`'s own call
chain (`fS_decoupled_from_preles_implementation_plan.md`). Under
`photosynthesis_as_input` (SPP) or `phydro`, `fS` silently stayed at `0.0`
all year, so any litter comparison under those two models would have been
driven by a constant `degree = 1` rather than a real seasonal signal. `fS`
is now computed once per day in `CASSIA.cpp`'s year loop regardless of
which photosynthesis model is active, with its own persistent state
(`growth_state.fS_temp_sum`) reset to the same `20.0` baseline PRELES
itself always used - `preles_cpp()` consumes that same shared value
instead of keeping its own copy, and its own output is confirmed
byte-identical to before this change. This section reruns Sect. 2's model
under SPP and p-hydro so Sect. 4 can compare all three photosynthesis
models' `needle_litter` against real data, not just PRELES.

`photosynthesis_as_input` (SPP) only has real driving data
(`weather_original`) for 2015-2017 - run over that narrow window only,
unlike PRELES's full 1998-2022 `weather_1998_2022`. `phydro`'s own ERA5
extraction (`ERA5_CASSIA_phydro.csv`) covers the full period like PRELES's
own file, so it is run over the same 1998-2022 window as Sect. 2's main
run - the litter comparisons below therefore show PRELES and p-hydro
across the full 2006-2016 funnel-trap window, and SPP only for the years
it actually has data for (2015-2016).

```{r three-models-weather}
data("weather_original")
weather_spp <- weather_original
weather_spp$dates <- as.Date(
  strptime(paste(rep(2015:2017, times = c(365, 366, 365)), weather_spp$X),
           format = "%Y %j"))
weather_spp <- weather_spp[format(weather_spp$dates, "%Y") %in% 2015:2016, ]

# p-hydro needs PPFD/PPFD_max/SWP/Nitrogen/PA, not in the PRELES file -
# Nitrogen/PA are placeholders (see phydro_version_comparison.Rmd).
weather_phydro_full <- data.table::fread("~/Documents/CASSIA/data/ERA5_CASSIA_phydro.csv")
names(weather_phydro_full)[names(weather_phydro_full) == "date"] <- "dates"
weather_phydro_full$dates    <- as.Date(weather_phydro_full$dates)
weather_phydro_full$Nitrogen <- 0.02
weather_phydro_full$PA       <- 101325
weather_phydro_full <- weather_phydro_full[
  weather_phydro_full$dates >= as.Date("1998-01-01") &
  weather_phydro_full$dates <= as.Date("2022-12-31"), ]
```

```{r three-models-runs}
run_leaf_mass <- function(weather, ...) {
  CASSIA_cpp(
    weather                    = weather,
    site                       = "Hyde",
    pPREL                      = c(parameters_2015$pPREL, parameters_2015$N_parameters),
    parameters                 = parameters_2015$parameters_test,
    common                     = common_p,
    ratios                     = ratios_p,
    sperling                   = parameters_2015$sperling_test,
    needle_mass_in             = 0,
    Throughfall                = parameters_2015$Throughfall,
    nitrogen_balance           = 25,
    organ_level_sugar          = FALSE,
    needle_mass_grows          = TRUE,
    height_diameter_correction = TRUE,
    leaf_mass_correction       = TRUE,
    root_turnover              = TRUE,
    ...
  )
}

# Both CASSIA_cpp() calls are wrapped in capture.output() to swallow the
# C++ solver's per-day Rcpp::Rcout diagnostics (CASSIA.cpp: "phydro solver
# returned a non-finite result..." when gpp/trans come back NaN and the
# previous day's values are reused as a fallback) - these are printed
# directly to stdout, not raised as R warning() conditions, so the
# chunk-level warning=FALSE option doesn't suppress them. Counted and
# summarised below instead of dumping one line per occurrence.
spp_log    <- capture.output(CASSIA_spp         <- run_leaf_mass(weather_spp, photosynthesis_as_input = TRUE))
phydro_log <- capture.output(CASSIA_phydro_full <- run_leaf_mass(weather_phydro_full, photosynthesis_as_input = FALSE, phydro = TRUE))
n_nonfinite_spp    <- sum(grepl("non-finite result", spp_log))
n_nonfinite_phydro <- sum(grepl("non-finite result", phydro_log))

# Converted to dry-mass-equivalent (/ carbon_share_hyde, Sect. 2's run-model
# chunk) for the same reason leaf_mass_df$litter was - matches the real
# karike data's native (oven-dried) units instead of leaving these in
# CASSIA's internal kg-carbon units.
spp_litter_df    <- data.frame(dates = weather_spp$dates,
                                litter        = CASSIA_spp$Turnover$needle_litter / carbon_share_hyde,
                                branch_litter = CASSIA_spp$Turnover$branch_litter / carbon_share_hyde,
                                cone_litter   = CASSIA_spp$Turnover$cone_litter   / carbon_share_hyde,
                                root_litter   = CASSIA_spp$Turnover$root_litter   / carbon_share_hyde)
spp_litter_df$year        <- as.integer(format(spp_litter_df$dates, "%Y"))
spp_litter_df$day_of_year <- as.integer(format(spp_litter_df$dates, "%j"))

phydro_litter_df <- data.frame(dates = weather_phydro_full$dates,
                                litter        = CASSIA_phydro_full$Turnover$needle_litter / carbon_share_hyde,
                                branch_litter = CASSIA_phydro_full$Turnover$branch_litter / carbon_share_hyde,
                                cone_litter   = CASSIA_phydro_full$Turnover$cone_litter   / carbon_share_hyde,
                                root_litter   = CASSIA_phydro_full$Turnover$root_litter   / carbon_share_hyde)
phydro_litter_df$year        <- as.integer(format(phydro_litter_df$dates, "%Y"))
phydro_litter_df$day_of_year <- as.integer(format(phydro_litter_df$dates, "%j"))

cat("SPP run window:    ", as.character(range(spp_litter_df$dates)), "\n")
cat("p-hydro run window:", as.character(range(phydro_litter_df$dates)), "\n")
cat("PRELES run window: ", as.character(range(leaf_mass_df$dates)), "\n")
cat(sprintf("SPP solver non-finite days (previous day's values used): %d\n", n_nonfinite_spp))
cat(sprintf("p-hydro solver non-finite days (previous day's values used): %d\n", n_nonfinite_phydro))
```

All three now land a single clean pulse in the day 250-290 window, close to
the real trap points - not the old flat, constant-`degree = 1` behavior SPP
and p-hydro would have shown before the fS decoupling fix. The models still
disagree on pulse timing/magnitude by a few days and up to ~2x in peak rate
(driven by each model's own GPP/growth trajectory feeding `max_leaf_mass_running`,
not by `fS` itself - all three now compute `fS` identically from the same
shared temperature-sum state) - a real difference worth tracking, visible
in Sect. 4 below.

## 3  trajectory - leaf_mass pool against its own target

```{r trajectory, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 7}
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = leaf_mass_df, aes(x = dates, y = leaf_mass),
            colour = "#1b7837", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_segment(data = n_repo_df, aes(x = start, xend = end, y = N_repo, yend = N_repo),
               colour = "#e08214", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = foliage_df, aes(x = dates, y = leaf_mass_kgC_tree),
             colour = okabe_ito_obs, size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "5 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(title = "leaf_mass pool vs. N_repo (yearly target) and real foliage biomass",
       subtitle = "1998-2022, Hyde-initialised, leaf_mass_correction = TRUE. Points: real pine_foliage_biomass stand inventories (CASSIA_Calibration/smearII_data), kg dry mass/ha -> kg C/tree.",
       x = NULL, y = "Needle leaf_mass (kg C / tree)") +
  pub_theme
```

---

## 4  Litter vs. real data, by component

`real_litter`/`comparison` were already prepared in Sect. 2.3;
`spp_litter_df`/`phydro_litter_df` in Sect. 2.4. The cumulative needle
data-vs-model comparison (previously its own two-panel figure here) is now
folded into Sect. 4.1's "Needles & leaves" panel and its printed totals -
no separate plot or statistic repeated in this section.

Cross-checked against Korhonen et al. (2013) - the same paper already
sourcing `theta_N_needles` - which independently reports annual N flux and
tissue N concentration per litter fraction (Sect. 3.6.1, Table 2) for this
exact site, letting a dry-mass rate be derived without touching the
funnel-trap spreadsheet at all:

```{r korhonen-litter-benchmark}
korhonen_litter <- data.frame(
  Component        = c("Needles", "Leaves", "Branches", "Bark", "Cones/seeds", "Other"),
  N_flux_kgN_ha_yr = c(8.0, 1.0, 5.3, 1.1, 0.35, 2.1),
  # Branches: text reports one combined flux (5.3) but Table 2 splits large
  # (4.7) vs small (4.4) branch N%; no split fraction given, so the mean of
  # the two is used as an approximation - flagged, not a precise figure.
  N_conc_mgN_g     = c(4.9, 8.8, mean(c(4.7, 4.4)), 3.7, 2.1, 12)
)
korhonen_litter$dry_mass_g_m2_yr <- korhonen_litter$N_flux_kgN_ha_yr /
  (korhonen_litter$N_conc_mgN_g / 1000) * 0.1  # kg N/ha/yr -> g dry mass/m2/yr
korhonen_litter <- korhonen_litter[order(-korhonen_litter$dry_mass_g_m2_yr), ]

karike_needle_g_m2_yr <- mean(aggregate(neulanen ~ year, data = real_litter, FUN = sum)$neulanen) / collector_area_m2
korhonen_needle_g_m2_yr <- korhonen_litter$dry_mass_g_m2_yr[korhonen_litter$Component == "Needles"]
cat("karike-derived needle rate:   ", round(karike_needle_g_m2_yr, 1), "g/m2/yr\n")
cat("Korhonen-derived needle rate:", round(korhonen_needle_g_m2_yr, 1), "g/m2/yr\n")
```

The two agree within ~15% (`r round(karike_needle_g_m2_yr,1)` vs
`r round(korhonen_needle_g_m2_yr,1)` g/m2/yr) - confirming the trap-geometry
and aggregation steps above are correct, and that the gap against CASSIA's
model is real rather than a unit artifact.

### 4.1  Cumulative totals, by component (2006-2016 funnel-trap window)

The `korhonen_litter` table above gives an independently-sourced rate for
every component below too (branches, bark, cones/seeds, leaves, other),
for cross-checking.

`karike_df_all` (`~/Documents/CASSIA_Calibration/Raw_Data/ancillary_ecosystem/`,
`Karikkeet_readme.txt`) separates every funnel-trap collection into
`neulanen` (needles), `kuori` (bark), `tikku` (twigs), `käpy` (cones),
`muu` (other) and `lehti` (leaves) - all six collected from the same
47.5cm funnel traps, so the same `collector_area_m2`/density conversion
above applies uniformly to each. CASSIA only ever models needle litter
(`leaf_mass_correction`'s own pathway) and root/mycorrhiza litter
(`root_turnover`, no funnel-trap equivalent exists for those - they're
belowground); cone litter has no modeled pathway at all (`grep`-confirmed
against `src/`: cones are mentioned only once, as a reference comment in
`sugar_model.cpp`), and branch litter is hardcoded to `0` in the C++
(`output_functions.cpp`: "no branch biomass pool") despite both being
real, measurable categories here. This isolates how much of the
needle-litter gap above is really a needle-specific shortfall versus how
big the *other* real components are in comparison.

Split below into a 2x2 grid, one panel per litter group, so a modeled
component's line always shares its data compartment's colour (black for
needles/needle_litter) rather than getting an unrelated colour of its
own; each panel's subtitle gives the matching cumulative 2006-2016 totals
for data vs. model. The needle_litter model line is further split by
linetype into PRELES and p-hydro (Sect. 2.4), both of which cover the
full 2006-2016 window. SPP is left out of this cumulative view - it only
has driving data for 2015-2016, so a `cumsum()` restricted to those two
years would restart at 0 instead of continuing from where PRELES/p-hydro's
2006-2014 accumulation already was, making its total look unfairly small
next to an 11-year cumulative. Sect. 4.2's day-of-year panel includes SPP
on equal footing, since a rate (not a running total) is comparable over
any sub-window.

```{r all-litter-components, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 13}
litter_components <- c(neulanen = "Needles", kuori = "Bark", tikku = "Twigs",
                        "käpy" = "Cones", muu = "Other", lehti = "Leaves")

component_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(litter_components), function(col) {
  df <- karike[!is.na(karike[[col]]) &
               format(karike$pvm, "%Y") %in% as.character(2006:2016),
               c("pvm", col)]
  names(df) <- c("pvm", "amount")
  agg <- aggregate(amount ~ pvm, data = df, FUN = mean)
  agg <- agg[order(agg$pvm), ]
  agg$year <- as.integer(format(agg$pvm, "%Y"))
  agg$trees_per_ha <- density_by_year[as.character(agg$year)]
  agg$kg_per_tree <- (agg$amount / collector_area_m2) / (agg$trees_per_ha / 10000) / 1000
  data.frame(pvm = agg$pvm, cum_kg_per_tree = cumsum(agg$kg_per_tree),
             total_kg_per_tree = sum(agg$kg_per_tree),
             Component = litter_components[[col]])
}))

totals_2006_2016 <- unique(component_long[, c("Component", "total_kg_per_tree")])
totals_2006_2016 <- totals_2006_2016[order(-totals_2006_2016$total_kg_per_tree), ]
cat("Real litter totals, 2006-2016, kg/tree (funnel-trap components, descending):\n")
print(totals_2006_2016, row.names = FALSE)

# Three-model needle_litter comparison (Sect. 2.4's spp_litter_df/phydro_litter_df,
# PRELES's own leaf_mass_df). Interval sums return NA outside a model's own
# run window (SPP: 2015-2016 only) rather than silently treating missing
# days as zero litter.
model_interval_sum2 <- function(start, end, litter_df) {
  if (is.na(start)) return(NA_real_)
  if (start < min(litter_df$dates) || end > max(litter_df$dates)) return(NA_real_)
  sum(litter_df$litter[litter_df$dates > start & litter_df$dates <= end])
}
real_litter$model_kg_per_tree_phydro <- mapply(model_interval_sum2, real_litter$interval_start, real_litter$pvm,
                                                MoreArgs = list(litter_df = phydro_litter_df))
real_litter$model_kg_per_tree_spp    <- mapply(model_interval_sum2, real_litter$interval_start, real_litter$pvm,
                                                MoreArgs = list(litter_df = spp_litter_df))
comparison     <- real_litter[!is.na(real_litter$model_kg_per_tree), ]
comparison_spp <- comparison[!is.na(comparison$model_kg_per_tree_spp), ]

# SPP excluded from the cumulative comparison: it only has driving data
# for 2015-2016, so its cumsum() necessarily restarts at 0 there instead
# of continuing from where PRELES/phydro's 2006-2014 accumulation already
# was - an apples-to-oranges "2-year cumulative" next to an "11-year
# cumulative" that would understate SPP's actual litter rate. Sect. 4.2's
# day-of-year panel compares all three models fairly (a rate, not a
# cumulative total), including SPP for the years it's run.
needle_model_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(pvm = comparison$pvm, cum_kg_per_tree = cumsum(comparison$model_kg_per_tree),
             Component = "Needles", Model = "PRELES"),
  data.frame(pvm = comparison$pvm, cum_kg_per_tree = cumsum(comparison$model_kg_per_tree_phydro),
             Component = "Needles", Model = "p-hydro")
)
model_linetypes <- c(PRELES = "solid", "p-hydro" = "dotted", SPP = "dashed")
model_linetypes_cumulative <- model_linetypes[c("PRELES", "p-hydro")]

# Branch litter (oksa), CASSIA_Calibration's own data - collected once a
# year from 0.5 m^2 ground frames, not the 47.5cm funnel traps, so its own
# area conversion applies (not collector_area_m2). Only covers 1997-2003
# (karike_df_all's oksa column), not the 2006-2016 window used above -
# plotted on its own window rather than forced onto the others'.
branch_frame_area_m2 <- 0.5
branch_real <- karike[!is.na(karike$oksa) &
                      format(karike$pvm, "%Y") %in% as.character(1997:2003),
                      c("pvm", "oksa")]
branch_agg <- aggregate(oksa ~ pvm, data = branch_real, FUN = mean)
branch_agg <- branch_agg[order(branch_agg$pvm), ]
branch_agg$year <- as.integer(format(branch_agg$pvm, "%Y"))
branch_agg$trees_per_ha <- density_by_year[as.character(branch_agg$year)]
branch_agg$kg_per_tree <- (branch_agg$oksa / branch_frame_area_m2) /
  (branch_agg$trees_per_ha / 10000) / 1000

branch_data_df <- data.frame(pvm = branch_agg$pvm,
                              cum_kg_per_tree = cumsum(branch_agg$kg_per_tree),
                              Component = "Branch litter")
branch_model_window <- leaf_mass_df[format(leaf_mass_df$dates, "%Y") %in% as.character(1997:2003), ]
branch_phydro_window <- phydro_litter_df[format(phydro_litter_df$dates, "%Y") %in% as.character(1997:2003), ]

# All three photosynthesis models give the same answer here (branch_litter
# is unconditionally hardcoded 0 - actual_growth.cpp, no standalone branch
# biomass pool exists yet) - shown per-model anyway, same as needle_litter
# above, so that's explicit rather than implied by a single line. SPP
# excluded: its own run only covers 2015-2016 (Sect. 2.4), no overlap at
# all with this 1997-2003 window (unlike needle_litter's panel, where SPP
# at least partially overlaps 2015-2016).
branch_model_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(pvm = branch_model_window$dates,
             cum_kg_per_tree = cumsum(branch_model_window$branch_litter),
             Component = "Branch litter", Model = "PRELES"),
  data.frame(pvm = branch_phydro_window$dates,
             cum_kg_per_tree = cumsum(branch_phydro_window$branch_litter),
             Component = "Branch litter", Model = "p-hydro")
)

# Root litter (root_turnover mechanism) - no funnel-trap root litter exists
# (belowground, uncollectable by the above-ground traps used for all other
# components here), so this is model output only, over the same 2006-2016
# window as Needles/Cones/etc. Same PRELES/p-hydro pair as needle_litter/
# branch_litter above (SPP excluded from this cumulative total - 2015-2016-
# only window vs. an 11-year cumulative, see Sect. 4.2).
root_model_window   <- leaf_mass_df[format(leaf_mass_df$dates, "%Y") %in% as.character(2006:2016), ]
root_phydro_window  <- phydro_litter_df[format(phydro_litter_df$dates, "%Y") %in% as.character(2006:2016), ]
root_model_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(pvm = root_model_window$dates,
             cum_kg_per_tree = cumsum(root_model_window$root_litter),
             Component = "Roots", Model = "PRELES"),
  data.frame(pvm = root_phydro_window$dates,
             cum_kg_per_tree = cumsum(root_phydro_window$root_litter),
             Component = "Roots", Model = "p-hydro")
)
root_model_total        <- sum(root_model_window$root_litter)
root_model_phydro_total <- sum(root_phydro_window$root_litter)

# Cone litter (masting-cycle mechanism) - ALL of the standing cone biomass
# (accumulated from real bud growth) sheds every n_age-th year (simulation
# year n_age, 2*n_age, 3*n_age, ... - 3/6/9 at Hyde, reusing the same n_age
# parameter needle_cohort_mass does, not a separate hardcoded cycle length),
# spread over a fixed day 121-273 window. Same 2006-2016 window and
# PRELES/p-hydro pair as Roots above.
cone_model_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(pvm = root_model_window$dates,
             cum_kg_per_tree = cumsum(root_model_window$cone_litter),
             Component = "Cones", Model = "PRELES"),
  data.frame(pvm = root_phydro_window$dates,
             cum_kg_per_tree = cumsum(root_phydro_window$cone_litter),
             Component = "Cones", Model = "p-hydro")
)
cone_model_total        <- sum(root_model_window$cone_litter)
cone_model_phydro_total <- sum(root_phydro_window$cone_litter)

needle_data_total   <- totals_2006_2016$total_kg_per_tree[totals_2006_2016$Component == "Needles"]
needle_preles_total <- sum(comparison$model_kg_per_tree)
needle_phydro_total <- sum(comparison$model_kg_per_tree_phydro)
needle_spp_total    <- sum(comparison_spp$model_kg_per_tree_spp)
leaves_data_total  <- totals_2006_2016$total_kg_per_tree[totals_2006_2016$Component == "Leaves"]
cones_data_total   <- totals_2006_2016$total_kg_per_tree[totals_2006_2016$Component == "Cones"]
twigs_data_total   <- totals_2006_2016$total_kg_per_tree[totals_2006_2016$Component == "Twigs"]
bark_data_total    <- totals_2006_2016$total_kg_per_tree[totals_2006_2016$Component == "Bark"]
branch_data_total  <- sum(branch_agg$kg_per_tree)
branch_model_total <- 0

cat("\nCumulative data vs. model totals (kg/tree):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Needles (2006-2016):       data = %.2f, model (needle_litter) = PRELES %.2f, p-hydro %.2f\n",
            needle_data_total, needle_preles_total, needle_phydro_total))
cat(sprintf("  (SPP excluded from this cumulative total - 2-year-only run vs. an 11-year total; see Sect. 4.2, SPP = %.2f kg/tree over 2015-2016)\n",
            needle_spp_total))
cat(sprintf("  Leaves  (2006-2016):       data = %.2f, model = not implemented\n", leaves_data_total))
cat(sprintf("  Cones   (2006-2016):       data = %.2f, model (cone_litter) = PRELES %.2f, p-hydro %.2f\n",
            cones_data_total, cone_model_total, cone_model_phydro_total))
cat(sprintf("  Twigs   (2006-2016):       data = %.2f, model = not implemented\n", twigs_data_total))
cat(sprintf("  Bark    (2006-2016):       data = %.2f, model = not implemented\n", bark_data_total))
cat(sprintf("  Branch litter (1997-2003): data = %.2f, model = %.2f (hardcoded 0)\n", branch_data_total, branch_model_total))
cat(sprintf("  Roots   (2006-2016):       data = not collected (belowground), model (root_litter) = PRELES %.2f, p-hydro %.2f\n",
            root_model_total, root_model_phydro_total))

# Colour-blind-safe (Okabe & Ito 2008). A modelled component reuses its data
# compartment's colour (Needles/needle_litter -> black; Branch litter ->
# magenta); linetype separates the model line (solid, or dashed for the
# always-0 branch output) from the unconnected data points.
component_colours <- c(
  Needles = "#000000", Leaves = "#F0E442", Cones = "#E69F00",
  Twigs = "#56B4E9", Bark = "#009E73",
  "Branch litter" = "#CC79A7", Roots = "#D55E00"
)

panel_theme <- pub_theme + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
wrap_sub <- function(...) paste(strwrap(sprintf(...), width = 48), collapse = "\n")

p_needles_leaves <- ggplot(mapping = aes(x = pvm, y = cum_kg_per_tree, colour = Component)) +
  geom_point(data = component_long[component_long$Component %in% c("Needles", "Leaves"),
                                    c("pvm", "cum_kg_per_tree", "Component")], size = 1.3) +
  geom_line(data = needle_model_long, aes(linetype = Model), linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = component_colours) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = model_linetypes_cumulative, name = "CASSIA model") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linetype = 0, shape = 16))) +  # Component = point only; CASSIA model = line only (separate legend)
  labs(title = "Needles & leaves",
       subtitle = wrap_sub("Needles - data: %.2f kg/tree. Model (needle_litter): PRELES %.2f, p-hydro %.2f. SPP excluded (2015-2016 only - see Sect. 4.2). Leaves - data: %.2f kg/tree, no CASSIA model.",
                           needle_data_total, needle_preles_total, needle_phydro_total, leaves_data_total),
       x = NULL, y = "Cumulative litter (kg / tree)") +
  panel_theme +
  theme(legend.box = "vertical")

p_cones <- ggplot(mapping = aes(x = pvm, y = cum_kg_per_tree, colour = Component)) +
  geom_point(data = component_long[component_long$Component == "Cones",
                                    c("pvm", "cum_kg_per_tree", "Component")], size = 1.3) +
  geom_line(data = cone_model_long, aes(linetype = Model), linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = component_colours) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = model_linetypes_cumulative, name = "CASSIA model") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linetype = 0, shape = 16))) +
  labs(title = "Cones",
       subtitle = wrap_sub("Data: %.2f kg/tree. Model (cone_litter, masting cycle - all standing cone biomass sheds every 3rd year): PRELES %.2f, p-hydro %.2f. SPP excluded (2015-2016 only - see Sect. 4.2).",
                           cones_data_total, cone_model_total, cone_model_phydro_total),
       x = NULL, y = "Cumulative litter (kg / tree)") +
  panel_theme +
  theme(legend.box = "vertical")

p_twigs_bark <- ggplot(component_long[component_long$Component %in% c("Twigs", "Bark"),
                                       c("pvm", "cum_kg_per_tree", "Component")],
                        aes(x = pvm, y = cum_kg_per_tree, colour = Component)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = component_colours) +
  labs(title = "Twigs & bark",
       subtitle = wrap_sub("Twigs - data: %.2f kg/tree, no CASSIA model. Bark - data: %.2f kg/tree, no CASSIA model.",
                           twigs_data_total, bark_data_total),
       x = NULL, y = "Cumulative litter (kg / tree)") +
  panel_theme

p_branch <- ggplot(mapping = aes(x = pvm, y = cum_kg_per_tree, colour = Component)) +
  geom_point(data = branch_data_df, size = 1.3) +
  geom_line(data = branch_model_long, aes(linetype = Model), linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = component_colours) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = model_linetypes_cumulative, name = "CASSIA model") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linetype = 0, shape = 16))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(title = "Branch litter",
       subtitle = wrap_sub("1997-2003 (own window, not funnel traps). Data (oksa, 0.5 m^2 ground frames): %.2f kg/tree. Model (PRELES/p-hydro, SPP has no overlap): %.2f kg/tree (hardcoded 0, no branch biomass pool).",
                           branch_data_total, branch_model_total),
       x = NULL, y = "Cumulative litter (kg / tree)") +
  panel_theme +
  theme(legend.box = "vertical")

p_roots <- ggplot(mapping = aes(x = pvm, y = cum_kg_per_tree, colour = Component)) +
  geom_line(data = root_model_long, aes(linetype = Model), linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = component_colours) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = model_linetypes_cumulative, name = "CASSIA model") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linetype = 0, shape = 16))) +
  labs(title = "Roots",
       subtitle = wrap_sub("No funnel-trap root litter data exists (belowground). Model (root_litter, root_turnover mechanism): PRELES %.2f, p-hydro %.2f. SPP excluded (2015-2016 only - see Sect. 4.2).",
                           root_model_total, root_model_phydro_total),
       x = NULL, y = "Cumulative litter (kg / tree)") +
  panel_theme +
  theme(legend.box = "vertical")

(p_needles_leaves | p_cones) / (p_twigs_bark | p_branch) / (p_roots | plot_spacer()) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Cumulative real litterfall by component, 2006-2016",
    subtitle = paste(strwrap(
      "Real: discrete SMEAR karike funnel-trap collections (points). CASSIA: modeled litter outputs (lines), coloured to match their data compartment; needle_litter/cone_litter/branch_litter/root_litter's PRELES/p-hydro all separated by linetype under the same \"CASSIA model\" legend (SPP excluded from every cumulative panel - unfair over a partial 2015-2016 window, see Sect. 4.2). Roots: model only, no comparable data (belowground, not captured by the above-ground traps).",
      width = 110), collapse = "\n"),
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
  )
```

**Branch litter (`oksa`), now included above on its own window.** Per
`Karikkeet_readme.txt`, branches are collected once a year from 0.5 m²
ground frames, not the funnel traps - a different area (`branch_frame_area_m2`
above, not `collector_area_m2`) and a different sampling frequency from the
other five components. Coverage is also much shorter and non-overlapping
with the 2006-2016 window used for Needles/Leaves/Cones/Twigs/Bark
(`karike_df_all`'s `oksa` column: 1997-05-30 to 2003-08-04 only, 192 rows,
plotted against the model's hardcoded-0 output over that same 1997-2003
span). A real, measured litter category CASSIA currently models as a
hardcoded zero - the panel above is the dedicated comparison flagged
previously, confirming there is a real, non-trivial branch litter signal
(`r round(branch_data_total, 2)` kg/tree, 1997-2003) that a future
branch-litter mechanism would need to reproduce.

### 4.2  Cumulative litter by day-of-year, by component (faceted by year)

Same 5-component split and colour scheme as Sect. 4.1 (stacked, not the
2x3 grid - each panel already facets by year internally), faceted by year
instead of one continuous 2006-2016 line - each facet is that single
year's own cumulative total, restarting at `0` on Jan 1, so the timing
*within* a year (and its year-to-year variability) is visible rather than
blurring into one long multi-year curve. Snapshot of what each panel
shows as of this session:

- **Needles & leaves**: all three photosynthesis models for
  `needle_litter`, with SPP only appearing in the 2015/2016 facets it
  actually has driving data for. Current formula (C++, Sect. 5): a
  skew-normal timing shape (`omega_litter`, `alpha_litter`, one-year-lagged
  `xi_litter`) normalised against last year's running total, scaled by
  this year's needle-cohort magnitude (`needle_cohort_mass` - Repola-
  initialised, rolled over by `n_age` each year).
- **Cones**: real data plus `cone_litter`, all three photosynthesis models
  (C++, masting cycle - standing cone biomass accumulates from real bud
  growth; ALL of it sheds every `n_age`-th simulation year (year 3, 6,
  9, ... at Hyde, same per-site cycle length needle cohorts use), spread
  over the same fixed day 121-273 window Sect. 5.2's RMSE-fitting
  exercise originally identified). An independent magnitude now, not
  scaled to each year's observed total. SPP only appears in the
  2015/2016 facets it actually has driving data for, same as Needles.
- **Twigs & bark**: real data only, no CASSIA model - informational,
  not a current modelling priority.
- **Branch litter**: real data (1997-2003 window) against the model's
  hardcoded-0 output, PRELES/p-hydro (SPP has no overlap with this
  window). TODO: crown height - branch litter should be added alongside
  crown height work, not on its own.
- **Roots**: model output only (`root_litter`, `root_turnover`
  mechanism), all three photosynthesis models - no comparable data
  exists (belowground, not captured by the above-ground funnel traps).

Shaded bands mark the peak litterfall month(s) reported for each
fraction at this exact site by Portillo-Estrada, Korhonen, Pihlatie,
Pumpanen, Frumau, Morillas, Tosens & Niinemets (2013) (full citation in
References below) - needle Aug-Oct (varies by year), cones/seeds Jun-Jul,
twigs May (plus event-driven winter-storm secondary peaks, not a fixed
calendar window so not shaded here), and bark with "no specific pattern"
- more evenly spread across the year, which is why its panel has no
shaded band. Their Table 4 needle rate (1,600 +/- 120 kg/ha/yr) is close
to the `karike`-derived rate over the same overlap years (~1,736
kg/ha/yr, 2006-2011) - close enough that this is very likely the same
underlying long-term Hyytiälä litter-trap programme `karike_df_all`
draws from, rather than an independent dataset.

```{r litter-cumulative-by-component-year, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 38}
# Real cumulative amount per component, within each component's own
# non-NA collection dates (mirrors real_litter's own kg_per_tree
# derivation in Sect. 2.3, generalised across all funnel-trap columns),
# cumulative *within* each year (resets to 0 each Jan 1).
component_daily <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(litter_components), function(col) {
  df <- karike[!is.na(karike[[col]]) &
               format(karike$pvm, "%Y") %in% as.character(2006:2016),
               c("pvm", col)]
  names(df) <- c("pvm", "amount")
  agg <- aggregate(amount ~ pvm, data = df, FUN = mean)
  agg <- agg[order(agg$pvm), ]
  agg$year           <- as.integer(format(agg$pvm, "%Y"))
  agg$trees_per_ha   <- density_by_year[as.character(agg$year)]
  agg$kg_per_tree    <- (agg$amount / collector_area_m2) / (agg$trees_per_ha / 10000) / 1000
  agg$day_of_year    <- as.integer(format(agg$pvm, "%j"))
  agg$year_label      <- year_label(agg$year)
  agg$cum_kg_per_tree <- ave(agg$kg_per_tree, agg$year, FUN = cumsum)
  data.frame(pvm = agg$pvm, year_label = agg$year_label, day_of_year = agg$day_of_year,
             cum_kg_per_tree = agg$cum_kg_per_tree,
             Component = litter_components[[col]])
}))

# Cross-check against Portillo-Estrada et al. (2013)'s reported Dec-Feb
# litterfall minimum (0.078-0.127 g/m2/day, all fractions; needles ~40+/-17%
# of that at the minima) - addresses the earlier-onset finding (real
# needle litter is already falling well before CASSIA's day>212 gate).
needle_g_m2_day <- karike[!is.na(karike$neulanen) &
                          format(karike$pvm, "%Y") %in% as.character(2006:2016), ]
needle_g_m2_day <- aggregate(neulanen ~ pvm, data = needle_g_m2_day, FUN = mean)
needle_g_m2_day <- needle_g_m2_day[order(needle_g_m2_day$pvm), ]
needle_g_m2_day$doy <- as.integer(format(needle_g_m2_day$pvm, "%j"))
needle_g_m2_day$interval_days <- as.numeric(needle_g_m2_day$pvm - c(as.Date(NA), head(needle_g_m2_day$pvm, -1)))
needle_g_m2_day$rate <- (needle_g_m2_day$neulanen / collector_area_m2) / needle_g_m2_day$interval_days
needle_before212_g_m2_day <- needle_g_m2_day$rate[needle_g_m2_day$doy <= 212 & !is.na(needle_g_m2_day$rate)]

cat("karike needle background rate before day 212 (g/m2/day): median =",
    round(median(needle_before212_g_m2_day), 3), ", mean =", round(mean(needle_before212_g_m2_day), 3), "\n")
cat("Portillo-Estrada et al. (2013) implied needle winter (Dec-Feb) minimum: 0.031-0.051 g/m2/day\n")
cat("(same order of magnitude - the early background signal is a real, literature-corroborated effect)\n")

# Same three models as Sect. 4.1, cumulative *within* each year instead
# of across the full 2006-2016 range; restricting to 2006-2016 naturally
# keeps SPP's two available years (2015-2016) and drops the rest, with no
# special-casing.
needle_day_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(leaf_mass_df[leaf_mass_df$year %in% 2006:2016, c("year", "day_of_year", "litter")], Model = "PRELES"),
  data.frame(phydro_litter_df[phydro_litter_df$year %in% 2006:2016, c("year", "day_of_year", "litter")], Model = "p-hydro"),
  data.frame(spp_litter_df[spp_litter_df$year %in% 2006:2016, c("year", "day_of_year", "litter")], Model = "SPP")
)
needle_day_long$year_label <- year_label(needle_day_long$year)
needle_day_long$Component  <- "Needles"
needle_day_long$cum_litter <- ave(needle_day_long$litter, interaction(needle_day_long$year, needle_day_long$Model),
                                   FUN = cumsum)

# Branch litter's own 1997-2003 window/area (Sect. 4.1), cumulative within
# each year.
branch_daily <- karike[!is.na(karike$oksa) &
                       format(karike$pvm, "%Y") %in% as.character(1997:2003),
                       c("pvm", "oksa")]
branch_daily_agg <- aggregate(oksa ~ pvm, data = branch_daily, FUN = mean)
branch_daily_agg <- branch_daily_agg[order(branch_daily_agg$pvm), ]
branch_daily_agg$year           <- as.integer(format(branch_daily_agg$pvm, "%Y"))
branch_daily_agg$trees_per_ha   <- density_by_year[as.character(branch_daily_agg$year)]
branch_daily_agg$kg_per_tree    <- (branch_daily_agg$oksa / branch_frame_area_m2) /
  (branch_daily_agg$trees_per_ha / 10000) / 1000
branch_daily_agg$day_of_year    <- as.integer(format(branch_daily_agg$pvm, "%j"))
branch_daily_agg$year_label      <- as.character(branch_daily_agg$year)
branch_daily_agg$cum_kg_per_tree <- ave(branch_daily_agg$kg_per_tree, branch_daily_agg$year, FUN = cumsum)
branch_daily_df <- branch_daily_agg
branch_daily_df$Component <- "Branch litter"

)

day_panel_theme <- panel_theme + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8))

# Literature peak-month windows (Portillo-Estrada et al. 2013, Hyytiälä),
# shaded behind the data in each relevant panel - lacking the year_label
# facet column, so ggplot replicates each rect across every year facet.
# Darker fill + a dashed border (vs. the original plain grey50/alpha=0.12)
# so the band reads clearly even next to the grid lines/points.
lit_band <- function(start_doy, end_doy) {
  list(
    geom_rect(data = data.frame(xmin = start_doy, xmax = end_doy, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
              aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "#B0B0B0", alpha = 0.35),
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(start_doy, end_doy), linetype = "22", colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.4)
  )
}

p_needles_leaves_day <- ggplot() +

constant_shape <- function(day, p) {  # kept for Sect. 5.2's shape comparison, re-used as-is

  end <- start + duration - 1

}

# Same three-model pattern as Roots/Needles above.
cone_day_long <- rbind(

p_branch_day <- ggplot(branch_daily_df, aes(x = day_of_year, y = cum_kg_per_tree, colour = Component)) +

p_needles_leaves_day / p_cones_day / p_twigs_bark_day / p_branch_day / p_roots_day +

    subtitle = "Real: karike funnel-trap cumulative totals (points), faceted by year - each facet restarts at 0 on Jan 1. Shaded bands: Portillo-Estrada et al. (2013) literature peak months, per panel. Needles/Cones/Branch litter/Roots all show PRELES/p-hydro/SPP under the same \"CASSIA model\" legend (SPP only where it has driving data, 2015-2016). Roots: model only, no comparable data.",
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

```

The printed comparison above speaks to the earlier-onset question from this session: CASSIA's needle_litter mechanism *was* hard-gated to exactly `0` before day 212 (`degree = max(0, 1 - fS^2)`, `day > 212`), but the real `karike` data already has a non-trivial background rate before that gate opens (median `r round(median(needle_before212_g_m2_day), 3)` g/m2/day across 2006-2016) - and Portillo-Estrada et al. (2013) independently corroborates this isn't a sampling artifact at this site: their Dec-Feb litterfall minimum (0.078-0.127 g/m2/day, all fractions combined) with needles at ~40+/-17% of that minimum implies a literature-sourced needle winter rate of 0.031-0.051 g/m2/day - the same order of magnitude as the `karike`-derived figure above, from a dataset spanning different (if likely overlapping) years. The autumn **peak** timing was well supported (both this paper's Aug-Oct range and Starr et al.'s day 250-290 bracket the old mechanism's pulse), but the hard pre-212 zero was the part without literature support. **This is exactly what Sect. 5.1's skew-normal mechanism (now live in `actual_growth.cpp`, replacing the day-212 gate entirely) fixes** - its fitted shape already puts ~26-28% of the annual total before day 212, matching this real background rather than a background term bolted on separately.

The black dashed lines in the Needles panel above (day 150/300) are a visual estimate of the real data's own onset/tail-off, not a literal CASSIA parameter - the new skew-normal mechanism no longer uses any single fixed calendar day at all (its location `xi` shifts every year from the prior year's `fS` signal, Sect. 5.1), so there is no one "day in the code" left to mark with a single line the way the old day-212 gate had.

### 4.3  Next steps: calibrating needles, roots, and branches against real data

Needles are the only litter stream validated against real data above.
Two more are wanted:

- **Roots.** No litter-trap equivalent exists - Korhonen et al. (2013)
  explicitly excluded fine roots from this same study's scope ("litter
  traps don't catch root turnover"), so neither 4.1 nor 4.2 above can be
  reused for root litter directly. Real magnitude and turnover-time
  numbers do exist, though (no within-year seasonal curve found - only
  annual totals and a mycelia summer/winter split):
    - **Magnitude**: Ding et al. (2021, *Forest Ecology and Management*
      489:119081) - four southern-Finland Scots pine sites along a
      fertility gradient (CTY/CT/VT/MT), litter-trap (AG) and
      minirhizotron-based (BG) measurements. Total annual litter
      (AG + BG) was 206.2/276.2/307.1 g C/m^2 for CT/VT/MT;
      **belowground (BG) litter alone was 70-91 g C/m^2/yr**, of which
      ectomycorrhizal (EcM) mycelia production was only 8-13% - the rest
      is fine-root litter/exudates, i.e. roughly 61-84 g C/m^2/yr is
      fine-root-specific. AG litter was 1.7-3.3x higher than BG across
      sites (131-236 vs. 70-91 g/m^2/yr per the abstract).
    - **Turnover time**: the same paper's Table 3 (Kaplan-Meier median
      fine-root longevity, pine) gives 324/881/367/487 days (~0.89/2.41/
      1.01/1.33 years) for CTY/CT/VT/MT respectively - not Hyytiälä
      itself, but the same species, region, and order of magnitude as
      `parameters_p`'s own `root.lifetime` (1.7 years, Hyde).
    - **A real, actionable gap this surfaces**: `root_turnover`'s own
      turnover-time constant (`actual_growth.cpp`) is a hardcoded `3.0`
      placeholder ("matching needle longevity's default... TODO: ideally
      `parameters.root_lifetime` once that's actually populated") - but
      `root.lifetime` **is** already populated (1.7 years, Hyde) and
      simply isn't being read by `root_turnover` at all. Wiring that up
      would be a direct, low-effort step toward real root litter
      calibration, independent of finding more data.
    - Other candidate sources not yet pulled numbers from:
      `CASSIA_Calibration/Raw_Data/ryhti_data/` (root litter
      decomposition rates, not production magnitude) and the
      Helmisaari/Ostonen fine-root biomass literature already cited
      elsewhere in this project.
- **Branches.** CASSIA has no branch litter mechanism at all right now
  (`output_functions.cpp`: hardcoded to `0`, "no branch biomass pool") -
  calibrating this means building that mechanism first, not just
  updating a validation plot. Sect. 4.1/4.2's branch panels already plot
  one real candidate target (`karike_df_all`'s `oksa` column, 1997-2003,
  ground-frame collection); Korhonen's independent branch rate (Sect. 4
  above, ~117 g/m2/yr, blended large/small branch N%) is a second
  cross-check once a mechanism exists to calibrate.

Both are future work, not attempted in this session.

---

## 5  Alternative bell shapes for the litter pulse: fitting comparison

```{r shape-candidates}
makela_bell <- function(s, p) {
  sLc <- p[1]
  out <- numeric(length(s))
  valid <- s > 0 & s < sLc^2
  out[valid] <- (sLc * sqrt(s[valid]) - s[valid]) / (sLc^2 / 4)
  out
}
gaussian_bell <- function(s, p) {
  mu <- p[1]; sigma <- p[2]
  exp(-(s - mu)^2 / (2 * sigma^2))
}
triangular_bell <- function(s, p) {
  width <- p[1]; peak <- p[2]
  out <- numeric(length(s))
  valid <- s > 0 & s < width
  out[valid] <- ifelse(s[valid] <= peak, s[valid] / peak, (width - s[valid]) / (width - peak))
  out
}
```

```{r shape-fit}
degree_full <- with(leaf_mass_df, ifelse(day_of_year > 212, pmax(0, 1 - fS^2), 0))
sL_full <- ave(degree_full, leaf_mass_df$year, FUN = cumsum)
shape_df <- data.frame(dates = leaf_mass_df$dates, year = leaf_mass_df$year,
                        degree = degree_full, s = sL_full)

rmse_cumulative <- function(params, shape_fn, years) {
  sq_errs <- c()
  for (yr in years) {
    yr_df <- shape_df[shape_df$year == yr, ]
    rate <- yr_df$degree * shape_fn(yr_df$s, params)
    total <- sum(rate)
    if (!is.finite(total) || total < 1e-8) return(10)  # degenerate params: heavy penalty
    cum_rate <- cumsum(rate) / total
    real_yr <- real_litter[real_litter$year == yr, ]
    real_total <- sum(real_yr$neulanen)
    if (real_total < 1e-8) next
    real_cum <- cumsum(real_yr$neulanen) / real_total
    model_at_real_dates <- sapply(real_yr$pvm, function(dt) {
      idx <- which(yr_df$dates == dt)
      if (length(idx) == 0) return(NA)
      cum_rate[idx]
    })
    valid <- !is.na(model_at_real_dates)
    sq_errs <- c(sq_errs, (model_at_real_dates[valid] - real_cum[valid])^2)
  }
  if (length(sq_errs) == 0) return(10)
  sqrt(mean(sq_errs))
}

fit_makela <- optimize(function(p) rmse_cumulative(p, makela_bell, train_years), interval = c(0.5, 10))
# Bounded (0.1-30, 0.3-20 / 0.5-30, 0.1-29.5): keeps the peak within the
# real accumulated-s range (~0-90) - unconstrained fits degenerate into a
# monotonic ramp (fitted mu far outside the data's range), the same
# failure mode the original g_cold exploration already hit (see plan doc).
fit_gauss <- optim(par = c(mu = 3, sigma = 2), fn = function(p) rmse_cumulative(p, gaussian_bell, train_years),
                    method = "L-BFGS-B", lower = c(0.1, 0.3), upper = c(30, 20))
fit_tri   <- optim(par = c(width = 5, peak = 2), fn = function(p) rmse_cumulative(p, triangular_bell, train_years),
                    method = "L-BFGS-B", lower = c(0.5, 0.1), upper = c(30, 29.5))
```

```{r shape-comparison-data}
example_year <- 2010  # a training year, for visual reference
yr_df <- shape_df[shape_df$year == example_year, ]

curve_df <- rbind(
  data.frame(dates = yr_df$dates, rate = yr_df$degree * makela_bell(yr_df$s, fit_makela$minimum),
             Shape = "Current (Makela bell)"),
  data.frame(dates = yr_df$dates, rate = yr_df$degree * gaussian_bell(yr_df$s, fit_gauss$par),
             Shape = "Gaussian"),
  data.frame(dates = yr_df$dates, rate = yr_df$degree * triangular_bell(yr_df$s, fit_tri$par),
             Shape = "Triangular")
)
curve_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(curve_df, curve_df$Shape), function(d) {
  d$rate_norm <- d$rate / sum(d$rate)
  d
}))

real_example <- real_litter[real_litter$year == example_year, ]
real_example$rate_norm <- real_example$neulanen / sum(real_example$neulanen)
```

### 5.1  A skewed distribution directly over day-of-year, no gate/accumulator at all

Tested here instead: drop the gate and the fS-based accumulator entirely,
and fit a single **skew-normal density directly over calendar
day-of-year** - `(2/omega) * dnorm((d-xi)/omega) * pnorm(alpha*(d-xi)/omega)`,
3 free parameters (`xi` location, `omega` scale, `alpha` skew), no `sLc`,
no `fS`, no `day > 212` gate. Fit with the same cumulative-proportion RMSE
procedure and the same train/validation year split as above, just
evaluated over `1:366` instead of the accumulated-`s` grid.

```{r skewnorm-candidate}
skew_normal_doy <- function(d, p) {
  xi <- p[1]; omega <- p[2]; alpha <- p[3]
  z <- (d - xi) / omega
  (2 / omega) * dnorm(z) * pnorm(alpha * z)
}

rmse_cumulative_doy <- function(params, shape_fn, years) {
  full_days <- 1:366
  rate  <- shape_fn(full_days, params)
  total <- sum(rate)
  if (!is.finite(total) || total < 1e-8) return(10)
  cum_rate <- cumsum(rate) / total
  sq_errs <- c()
  for (yr in years) {
    real_yr <- real_litter[real_litter$year == yr, ]
    real_total <- sum(real_yr$neulanen)
    if (real_total < 1e-8) next
    real_cum <- cumsum(real_yr$neulanen) / real_total
    sq_errs <- c(sq_errs, (cum_rate[real_yr$day_of_year] - real_cum)^2)
  }
  if (length(sq_errs) == 0) return(10)
  sqrt(mean(sq_errs))
}
```

```{r skewnorm-fit}
# A single starting point (xi=265, omega=40, alpha=-5) converges to a
# degenerate near-symmetric local optimum (alpha~0, collapsing to a plain
# wide Gaussian) - L-BFGS-B is gradient-based and gets stuck. Multi-start
# across a small grid of diverse starting points finds a meaningfully
# better, genuinely skewed optimum instead.
starts <- expand.grid(xi = c(230, 250, 270, 290), omega = c(10, 20, 40, 70),
                       alpha = c(-30, -10, -2, 0, 5, 20))
fits_skew <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(starts)), function(i) {
  tryCatch(optim(par = as.numeric(starts[i, ]),
                  fn = function(p) rmse_cumulative_doy(p, skew_normal_doy, train_years),
                  method = "L-BFGS-B", lower = c(150, 3, -80), upper = c(330, 150, 80)),
           error = function(e) NULL)
})
fits_skew <- fits_skew[!vapply(fits_skew, is.null, logical(1))]
fit_skew  <- fits_skew[[which.min(vapply(fits_skew, `[[`, numeric(1), "value"))]]

skew_validation_rmse <- rmse_cumulative_doy(fit_skew$par, skew_normal_doy, valid_years)
skew_pre212_share <- 100 * sum(skew_normal_doy(1:212, fit_skew$par)) / sum(skew_normal_doy(1:366, fit_skew$par))

cat("Fitted skew-normal: xi =", round(fit_skew$par[1], 1), " omega =", round(fit_skew$par[2], 1),
    " alpha =", round(fit_skew$par[3], 2), "\n")
cat(sprintf("Train RMSE = %.4f, Validation RMSE = %.4f\n", fit_skew$value, skew_validation_rmse))
cat(sprintf("Share of annual total falling before day 212: %.1f%% (gated shapes above: 0%% by construction; real karike data: ~14-33%%, pooled ~20%%)\n",
            skew_pre212_share))
```

### 5.2  Cone litter: a bud-growth-style fixed-window mechanism

```{r cone-bud-shape}
# constant_shape() and cone_par (day 121-273) are already defined in
# Sect. 4.2, where they're used to draw the Cones panel's model line -
# reused here as-is. half_sine_shape() is the bud-growth-style
# alternative being compared against it.
half_sine_shape <- function(day, p) {
  start <- p[1]; duration <- p[2]
  sB <- day + 1 - start
  out <- numeric(length(day))
  valid <- sB >= 0 & sB < duration
  out[valid] <- (sin(2 * pi / duration * (sB[valid] - duration / 4)) + 1) / 2
  out
}
```

```{r cone-real-data}
real_cones <- karike[!is.na(karike[["käpy"]]) &
                     format(karike$pvm, "%Y") %in% as.character(2006:2016),
                     c("pvm", "käpy")]
names(real_cones) <- c("pvm", "amount")
real_cones <- aggregate(amount ~ pvm, data = real_cones, FUN = mean)
real_cones <- real_cones[order(real_cones$pvm), ]
real_cones$year        <- as.integer(format(real_cones$pvm, "%Y"))
real_cones$day_of_year <- as.integer(format(real_cones$pvm, "%j"))
real_cones$year_label  <- year_label(real_cones$year)
```

```{r cone-bud-fit}
rmse_cumulative_cones <- function(params, shape_fn, years) {
  full_days <- 1:366
  rate <- shape_fn(full_days, params)
  total <- sum(rate)
  if (!is.finite(total) || total < 1e-8) return(10)
  cum_rate <- cumsum(rate) / total
  sq_errs <- c()
  for (yr in years) {
    real_yr <- real_cones[real_cones$year == yr, ]
    real_total <- sum(real_yr$amount)
    if (real_total < 1e-8) next
    real_cum <- cumsum(real_yr$amount) / real_total
    sq_errs <- c(sq_errs, (cum_rate[real_yr$day_of_year] - real_cum)^2)
  }
  if (length(sq_errs) == 0) return(10)
  sqrt(mean(sq_errs))
}

cat("Cone window (set, not fit, Sect. 4.2): start =", cone_par[["start"]],
    "(May 1), end =", cone_par[["start"]] + cone_par[["duration"]] - 1, "(Sep 30)\n")
cat(sprintf("Half-sine: train RMSE = %.4f, validation RMSE = %.4f\n",
            rmse_cumulative_cones(cone_par, half_sine_shape, train_years),
            rmse_cumulative_cones(cone_par, half_sine_shape, valid_years)))
cat(sprintf("Constant:  train RMSE = %.4f, validation RMSE = %.4f\n",
            rmse_cumulative_cones(cone_par, constant_shape, train_years),
            rmse_cumulative_cones(cone_par, constant_shape, valid_years)))
```

The constant rate actually wins: validation RMSE 0.165 vs. the half-sine's
0.183 (training RMSE 0.156 vs. 0.161). Bud growth's bell shape makes
sense for an organ that grows gradually then stops; cone drop looks
closer to "once the window opens, cones fall at a roughly steady rate
until it closes" - a uniform rate is both simpler and a better match once
the window itself is already set from the real data rather than fit.

## Parameters introduced this session

| Parameter | Value (Hyde) | Site-specific? | Meaning | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `omega_litter` | 83.3 | Yes (NA elsewhere) | Skew-normal scale (days) for `needle_litter`'s day-of-year timing | **Live in C++** (`actual_growth.cpp`, `parameters_p` row 86) |
| `alpha_litter` | -25.22 | Yes (NA elsewhere) | Skew-normal shape/skewness for `needle_litter` | **Live in C++** (row 87) |
| `xi_offset_litter` | 4.8 days | Yes (NA elsewhere) | Added to the prior year's `fS < 0.5` crossing day to get this year's skew-normal location (`xi_litter`) | **Live in C++** (row 88) |
| `sLc_litter` | 2.163312 | Yes (NA elsewhere) | Width of the retired fS^2-accumulator/Makela-bell mechanism `omega_litter`/`alpha_litter`/`xi_offset_litter` replaced | **Vestigial** - no longer read by any C++ code; kept in `parameters_p` (row 79) only so the Sect. 5.1 old-vs-new comparison can still reproduce the retired baseline |
| Cone litter window start | day 121 (May 1) | - | Fixed start of `cone_litter`'s shedding window (`cone_par["start"]`, Sect. 5.2) | **Live in C++** (`actual_growth.cpp`, hardcoded - no dedicated parameter yet) |
| Cone litter window duration | 153 days (end day 273, Sep 30) | - | Fixed duration of the same window | **Live in C++** (hardcoded) |
| Cone litter shape | Constant (uniform) rate | - | Winning shape within the fixed window (beat the bud-growth-style half-sine), Sect. 5.2 | **Live in C++** (hardcoded) |
| Masting period | `n_age` (3 Hyde, 5 Vario) | Yes | `cone_biomass_standing` sheds litter every `n_age`-th simulation year - year 3, 6, 9, ... at Hyde (`growth.cpp`'s `years_since_masting`) | **Live in C++** - reuses the existing `n_age` parameter (not a separate hardcoded constant), so the period is site-dynamic; still not calibrated against real masting-interval data |
| Masting shed fraction | 1 (all of it) | - | Fraction of `cone_biomass_standing` shed on a masting year - a mature cone is a discrete unit, so nothing is retained fractionally | **Live in C++** (hardcoded placeholder, not calibrated) |

The first three (needle litter) and the last three (cone litter) are all genuinely in the compiled model now (a fresh `devtools::load_all()`/install will pick them up). Cone litter's magnitude comes from real bud growth (`out.culm_growth.bud`, the same per-year running total needle litter's cohorts read from `out.culm_growth.needles`) - see Sect. 5.2 for the window/shape validation this reuses, and `development_notebooks/leaf_mass_correction.Rmd` Sect. 4.1/4.2 for the resulting `cone_litter` vs. real `käpy` data comparison. The masting period (now `n_age`, dynamic per site) and shed fraction (100%) are both still placeholders in the sense that neither has been fitted/calibrated against real cone-production data - reusing `n_age` removes the second hardcoded magic number, but doesn't make 3/5 years the *correct* masting interval, just the same site-specific number CASSIA already trusted for needle longevity.
